cards.title: Full Ownership of Dog Care & Ending the Mental Burden

items.label: Proactive Daily Routine
items.text: Take full, unprompted ownership of her daily essentials—walking her at least once every day and making sure she is fed every evening. If he cannot do it himself, it is his responsibility to reach out and arrange backup coverage beforehand, rather than letting it default to Mom.

items.label: Medical Follow-Through
items.text: Take initiative to call, schedule, and follow through on her spay appointment.

items.label: Hygiene & Mess Accountability
items.text: Actively handle the cleanup when she makes a mess on the couch or bleeds during heat cycles, rather than walking past it and leaving the physical labor to Mom.

cards.title: Independent Nighttime Routine & Honoring Bedtime Boundaries

items.label: Self-Initiated Timeline
items.text: Initiate and complete all evening responsibilities and bedtime prep well before the 12:30am internet cut-off, without Mom having to nag or track them down. Should be in rooms with all things done by 1:30am.

items.label: Hygiene Consistency
items.text: Make nightly tooth brushing a non-negotiable personal habit rather than an overlooked step that Mom has to verify or repeat herself about.

items.label: Ending Post-Cut-Off Lingering
items.text: Cut out the pattern of scrounging for food, congregating on the couch, watching TV, and chatting after 12:30am before all evening chores done. Late snacks and winding down need to happen within a reasonable evening window so they head to bed on a predictable schedule.

items.label: The Emotional Boundary / Core Need
items.text: Relief from feeling like a broken record every single night. Establishing structure and maturity so their late-night habits stop disrupting the peace of the home and draining parental energy while also not being respectful of their sleep and clear-headedness.

items.label: Daily Communication Checks
items.text: Log in and actively check emails and messages without waiting for Mom to give reminders or monitor the screen.

items.label: Clear Accountability Before Outings
items.text: Stay fully caught up on schoolwork before leaving for recreational activities like rock climbing. If something is falling behind, take the initiative to communicate the exact situation proactively—stating what is unfinished and committing to a clear completion timeline beforehand.

items.label: The Emotional Boundary / Core Need
items.text: Moving away from hand-holding and oversight. Fostering personal integrity and transparency so you aren't put in the exhausting role of academic enforcer right before he walks out the door to have fun.

cards.title: Clear Permission for Outings & Honoring Food Boundaries

items.label: Direct Parental Permission for Plans
items.text: Check directly with parents before confirming outings or leaving to go climbing with Brighton, rather than treating Brighton’s invitation as automatic permission.

items.label: Brighton’s Role & Buy-In
items.text: Ensure Brighton understands that an invitation or a ride from him does not bypass Mom and Dad; Brighton must reinforce that Ephraim gets direct parental clearance first.

items.label: Treats & Junk Food Integrity
items.text: Obtain direct permission for treats outside the usual family diet, or strictly honor an agreed-upon weekly allotment without sneaking, cheating, or negotiating extra.

cards.title: Personal Bedroom Standards: Daily Maintenance & Weekly Resets

items.label: Daily Non-Negotiable Upkeep
items.text: Keep personal spaces baseline functional every single day without being prompted. Never leave damp or wet laundry sitting on the floor—it goes directly into the laundry basket. Bring all used dishes, glasses, and mugs downstairs daily. Empty bedroom trash cans whenever they are full.

items.label: Weekly Deep Clean
items.text: Complete a thorough weekly reset of the bedroom, going beyond surface clutter to dust surfaces, wipe down needed areas, and vacuum floors.

cards.title: Household Contribution: Proactive Daily Support & Picking Up the Slack

items.label: Daily Action on Extra & Paid Chores
items.text: Step forward voluntarily every day to complete a share of the extra general chores and available paid tasks, taking full responsibility to execute them thoroughly.

items.label: Responsiveness to Parental Requests
items.text: While direct requests from Mom or Dad will happen and require immediate follow-through without pushback, the default expectation is unprompted, proactive ownership rather than waiting to be asked.

cards.title: Personal Hygiene & Self-Care Standards: Baseline Ownership

items.label: Activity & Sweat Accountability
items.text: Ephraim must shower immediately upon returning home from the climbing gym. For everyone, anytime heavy activity or sweating occurs, it triggers an immediate requirement to either shower or, at the absolute minimum, strip down and change into completely clean clothes, including fresh underwear.

items.label: Daily Clothing Resets & Underwear Standards
items.text: Even on non-shower days, wearing yesterday’s clothes is unacceptable. Clean clothes must be put on daily, with changing underwear being non-negotiable.

items.label: Daily Odor Control
items.text: Acknowledge when smelly, and use deodorant.

sections.title: Husband Action & Accountability: Home Winterization & Fatherhood Leadership

cards.title: Fatherhood Leadership: Guiding Ephraim's Character & Correcting Toxic Dynamics

items.label: Proactive Mentorship & Education
items.text: Take Ephraim's current attitudes, views, and behaviors seriously enough to do intentional reading/research before addressing him, rather than brushing it off as "just a phase" or waiting for a blowup.

items.label: Direct Father-to-Son Alignment
items.text: Sit down with Ephraim for a serious, grounded conversation about character and maturity. Clearly frame the standard: his current path and mindset are not shaping him into an honorable, mature man, and both parents are concerned about the trajectory he is choosing.

subitems.label: Putting an Immediate Stop to Teasing Oliver
subitems.text: Address and strictly forbid using clinical labels as weapons—specifically weaponizing "autistic" against Oliver.

subitems.label: Defending Mom's Honor
subitems.text: Shut down the constant undermining, disrespect, and habit of making fun of Mom. Set a firm example that speaking down to or mocking his mother is completely unacceptable in this house.
